elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms") and there is no mutual-written-agreement gate; the automatic-renewal conditions are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not 30, and no Vendor reminder), so the preferred path fails at element 1.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted language requires "Customer gives sixty (60) days written notice of non-renewal"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day ceiling. To reach preferred, change to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 4(a) as rendered contains no obligation on Kubient to notify or remind Customer before any renewal; no reminder mechanic was added.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Conditional trigger does not apply: neither the original nor the rendered paragraph 4(a) contains any renewal price-uplift or fee-adjustment mechanic, so no cap is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered text: "unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions or Customer gives sixty (60) days written notice of non-renewal" — a Customer non-renewal right with a 60-day window, at the fallback ceiling; deterministic check "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" returned ok.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the renewal clause permits no price increase on renewal, so no 5% cap language is needed and its absence is not a gap.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single inserted phrase creates the missing Customer non-renewal right at exactly 60 days, and the price-cap element is not triggered because paragraph 4(a) contains no renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred is not reached: the opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days and there is no Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal. To move to preferred, replace "sixty (60)" with "thirty (30)" and add an express Kubient reminder obligation not less than sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term.

Minimality holds: the edit adds only the operative words needed for the fallback element and deletes nothing. Vendor's separate 90-day post-Initial-Term convenience right, the material-breach mechanics, and the "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" allocation are all retained untouched, and the drafter correctly declined to touch the T4C notice period under this rule.

Intent preserved: the insertion sits inside the existing "unless" construction without breaking the "Term" definition parenthetical, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and non-renewal at natural term end does not contradict the retained sentence barring termination during the Initial Term (non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as a mid-term termination). If the drafter wants to remove any residual argument that a non-renewal notice served during the Initial Term is a prohibited "termination during the Initial Term," adding "effective at the end of the then-current Term" would be a clarifying, not required, tweak.
Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the edit the only exit was a 90-day convenience notice, so Customer had no non-renewal window at or under the 60-day fallback ceiling.
